hook.text: Enron's fraud couldn't have happened without banks. JPMorgan, Citibank.

buildup.text: Enron needed to hide debt to keep its stock price high.

discovery.text: JPMorgan used shell companies in the Cayman Islands called 'Mahonia' to funnel money as fake commodity trades to Enron.

twist.text: Banks paid $7.2 billion in settlements. They claimed they didn't know about the fraud.

climax.text: Enron was the fraud. Banks were the infrastructure. Without Wall Street's creative accounting.

punchline.text: $7.2 billion in fines. Banks built Enron's fraud infrastructure. They knew.

quiz.question: What role did banks play in Enron's fraud?
options: They designed financial structures to hide Enron's debt

details.summary: Major banks including JPMorgan, Citigroup, and Merrill Lynch helped Enron disguise billions in debt through complex structured finance transactions that made loans appear as legitimate trading revenue.
details.whyItMatters: Banks did not just fail to catch Enron's fraud; they actively designed the financial structures that made it possible. This complicity showed how banks can serve as architects of corporate deception.
takeaways: Banks designed prepay transactions that disguised loans as trades
JPMorgan and Citigroup paid over $300 million in settlements
Enron's collapse destroyed $74 billion in shareholder value

faq.question: How did banks help Enron hide its debt?
faq.answer: Banks structured commodity trades that were actually disguised loans. Enron recorded the cash inflows as trading revenue rather than debt, inflating its apparent profitability while hiding billions in obligations.

faq.question: Were bank employees punished for helping Enron?
faq.answer: Unlike Enron executives, very few bank employees faced criminal charges. Banks settled civil cases with regulators and investors, paying fines that were small relative to the profits they earned from the relationship.
